prompt.brief: Design a clinician-assistance platform that analyzes DICOM medical images and structured symptoms, produces evidence-linked suggestions with calibrated uncertainty, and preserves clinical oversight and privacy.
successSignals: Define patient/study identity, DICOM ingestion, clinical context, consent, model/version, evidence, uncertainty, review, and audit records.
Never present an unreviewed suggestion as a diagnosis; handle missing context, out-of-distribution images, bias, calibration, and urgent escalation.
Separate protected data ingestion from preprocessing, inference, clinician review, EHR integration, training, and immutable audit storage.
Explain PHI minimization, access controls, validation, rollback, downtime procedures, observability, and safe no-result behavior.

functional: Ingest and validate DICOM studies and permitted clinical context, run versioned analysis, and return findings, evidence regions, confidence, and limitations.
Support clinician review/override, symptom/context entry, FHIR/EHR exchange, worklists, urgent flags, and complete provenance.
Enforce consent and role access, preserve audit trails, retract/reprocess results, delete according to policy, and operate safely during outages.
nonFunctional: Meet validated per-condition sensitivity/specificity targets and expose uncertainty; keep routine study turnaround within the clinical SLA.
Process 1M studies per month with strict tenant/PHI isolation without a single hot key or unbounded synchronous work.
Do not lose committed state; make retries and duplicate events safe.
Degrade safely when downstream workers, caches, or external dependencies fail.
scaleAssumptions: 1M studies/month across 500 hospitals with PHI isolation
Partition by the primary tenant, user, item, or geographic key and isolate hot partitions.
Keep serving state bounded; retain raw events or durable records for replay and auditing.

deepDives.title: Consistency and idempotency
points: Keep the Clinician-assistance platform commit authoritative; let derived projections converge with visible version and freshness.
Use idempotency keys, conditional Clinician-assistance platform writes, event IDs, and versions so retries and replay are safe.
Return Clinician-assistance platform version and observedAt so clients can reason about freshness.

deepDives.title: Partitioning and hot keys
points: Partition Clinician-assistance platform by its primary read and write keys, then isolate hot tenants, users, items, or regions.
Bound Clinician-assistance platform work with backpressure and queue isolation so one hot key cannot dominate the cluster.
Keep a replay or reconciliation path for Clinician-assistance platform projection drift and partial failures.

deepDives.title: Failure and recovery
points: Serve the last acceptable Clinician-assistance platform projection or an explicit degraded response when workers fail.
Retain durable Clinician-assistance platform records for replay and make each downstream effect independently retryable.
Measure Clinician-assistance platform latency, backlog, freshness, error rate, and correctness drift.

tradeoffs.title: Strong consistency versus throughput
tradeoffs.recommendation: Strongly protect the business commit and use versioned eventual projections for high-volume reads.
tradeoffs.caution: Making every derived read synchronous increases coordination and tail latency.

tradeoffs.title: Push versus pull processing
tradeoffs.recommendation: Push bounded events to workers and pull durable snapshots on reads or recovery.
tradeoffs.caution: Unbounded fanout or full scans make bursts and hot keys expensive.

tradeoffs.title: Managed service versus custom control
tradeoffs.recommendation: Start with managed primitives where their limits match the access pattern, then isolate replaceable interfaces.
tradeoffs.caution: Provider defaults do not remove the need for quotas, replay, observability, and data lifecycle design.

commonMistakes: Putting all work on the synchronous request path.
Choosing a data store before writing the access patterns and consistency contract.
Ignoring retries, duplicate events, late data, deletion, privacy, or authorization.
Leaving hot partitions, backpressure, stale reads, and recovery unspecified.
Allowing unbounded requests or exports to compete with normal traffic.

followUps.question: What happens when the primary worker is unavailable?
followUps.answer: Acknowledge only after the durable boundary, serve the last acceptable projection, queue retryable work, and replay or reconcile after recovery.

followUps.question: How would you support a tenfold traffic spike?
followUps.answer: Pre-scale partitions, apply admission control and backpressure, isolate hot keys, cache immutable snapshots, and make freshness degradation visible.

followUps.question: How do you verify correctness?
followUps.answer: Use idempotency metrics, version gaps, sampled source-to-projection comparisons, replay tests, and a shadow rebuild before repair.
